topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by welcoming students and introducing the importance and notorious complexity of complement.

topics.label: Foundational principles of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts and operating logic of the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three pathways through which complement recognizes pathogens and initiates activation on target surfaces.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream mechanisms through which the complement cascade eliminates pathogens and drives inflammation.

topics.label: Regulation of complement on host cells
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the distinct clinical presentations and disease vulnerabilities resulting from genetic or acquired deficiencies in complement proteins.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the strategies pathogens use to circumvent complement attack, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary example.

topics.label: Closing remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by wrapping up complement and previewing the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
